claim: A relatively small reasoning ('thinking') model, Qwen3-8B, can outperform specially-trained LLM-as-a-Judge models up to 70B parameters at coding-task judgment, indicating reasoning capability matters more than raw parameter count or specialized judge training.
stance_target: model selection strategy for the software factory's code-review judge agent -- favoring reasoning-capable models over larger specially-trained judges purely for cost/resource optimization (pillar 6)
scope_conditions: CodeJudgeBench, 26 LLM-as-a-Judge models, code generation/repair/unit-test tasks, 2025
quoted_support: Notably, even relatively small thinking models, such as Qwen3-8B, can outperform specially trained LLM-as-a-Judge models up to 70B in size.

claim: Across all 26 benchmarked LLM-as-a-Judge models, simply swapping the order in which two code responses are presented in a pairwise comparison can substantially change the judgment accuracy, confirming position bias specifically in code-judging scenarios.
stance_target: assuming code-judging tasks are immune to the position bias documented in general text-judging benchmarks
quoted_support: For pairwise judging tasks, simply changing the order in which responses are presented can substantially impact accuracy... This sensitivity raises concerns about the reliability and consistency of LLM-as-a-Judge in coding scenarios.

claim: Pairwise comparison outperforms scalar point-wise judging, and retaining the full, unprocessed LLM response -- including comments and reasoning traces -- rather than stripping them before judging, improves LLM-as-a-Judge performance on coding tasks.
stance_target: concrete prompting-strategy recommendations for implementing the software factory's automated code-review judge
quoted_support: We find that using pair-wise comparison outperforms scalar point-wise judging. Furthermore, retaining comments and reasoning in the full, unprocessed LLM response leads to improved judge performance.

claim: CodeJudgeBench sources its 4,260 curated evaluation pairs from LiveCodeBench, which continually collects new problems from LeetCode, AtCoder, and CodeForces specifically to mitigate training-data contamination in coding benchmarks.
stance_target: methodology for building contamination-resistant rigid eval benchmarks for code-generating agents in the software factory
quoted_support: The problems come from LiveCodeBench, which mitigates data contamination by continually collecting new problems from platforms such as LeetCode, AtCoder, and CodeForces.

claim: LLM-as-a-Judge performance varies depending on which LLM originally generated the code or unit test being judged, meaning a judge model's accuracy is not uniform across different generator models.
stance_target: assuming a single validated judge model will perform uniformly well regardless of which generator agent in the software factory produced the code under review
quoted_support: when judging code and unit tests written by different LLMs, LLM-as-a-Judge models also show variance in performance.
